Wednesday, December 2, 2020  7:00 PM  Teleconference

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Mayor has called a special meeting of the City Council, to be called to
order via teleconference at 7:00 p.m. on Wednesday, December 2, 2020. The agenda for the special meeting with
the items of business to be transacted or discussed is set forth below.

Posted by the office of the City Clerk at 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, December 1, 2020.

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via
  teleconference.
  - City Council meeting videos are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.
  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 880 8899 8644 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)
  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.
  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.
  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 880 8899 8644, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.
  -Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  DECEMBER 2, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A Special meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:01 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
Order N-29-20.

1A.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

2.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

The City Council recessed to Closed Session at 7:04 p.m.

3.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4)
  Potential initiation of litigation: one potential case

The City Council reconvened from Closed Session at 7:38 p.m.

City Attorney Davis reported that the City Council took no reportable action on the Closed
Session item.

4.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  LOS ANGELES COUNTY HEALTH OFFICER ORDER – NEW RESTRICTIONS
  AND OUTDOOR DINING PROHIBITION

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL began a discussion regarding the differences between the
South Bay Cities Council of Government’s (SBCCOG) letter to the Los Angeles County
Board of Supervisors and the letter drafted by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL stated that she supports being a signatory to the SBCCOG
letter, and also supports sending the letter drafted by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted that the SBCCOG letter also requests additional funding
in support of restaurants and restaurant workers, which should be an important emphasis
added to the City’s letter as well.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN noted that he supports the SBCCOG’s letter, although it
contains less data and detail than his proposed letter. His letter was written in an effort to
advocate on behalf of the Peninsula communities whom he felt are being treated unfairly
through this process. He also noted that the three other Peninsula cities have preliminarily
approved the letter to be signed on behalf of all four cities. He stated that several Council
Members from Torrance also support the letter. He stated that his goal is for the County to
govern based on the eight individual districts they have created. He also clarified that the
SBCCOG’s letter discusses creating or joining an existing Health District, as opposed to his

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES – SPECIAL MEETING  1
DECEMBER 2, 2020
 letter which asks the County to govern based on their current structure of established
districts.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN agreed with COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF’s suggestion to
add into the letter the request for additional funding. He also agreed with COUNCIL
MEMBER ZERUNYAN in asking the County use its districts to govern, rather than form new
Health Districts.

MAYOR SCHMITZ thanked COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF for her efforts and representation of
the City with the SBCCOG. She clarified that the funding being requested by the SBCCOG
is actually a budgeted surplus in tax proceeds from the State of California funds. MAYOR
SCHMITZ also thanked COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN for creating a professional and
respectful letter using the County’s own data and asking them to operate within the
parameters with which they have already defined. She stated that she is in support of the
SBCCOG’s letter, as well as the City’s proposed letter in collaboration with the other
Peninsula cities.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL stated that she is in support of sending the letter with the
discussed changes.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT THE CITY MANAGER TO DRAFT A LETTER IN COORDINATION
  WITH ALL PENINSULA CITY MANAGERS TO THE LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS REQUESTING A MORE REGIONAL
  APPROACH TO THE PUBLIC HEALTH CRISIS AND LIFTING THE
  TEMPORARY OUTDOOR DINING BAN, AND TO REQUEST ADDITIONAL
  STATE FUNDING TO THE EXTENT IT IS AVAILABLE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Manager Grammer noted that the City is making efforts to support local restaurants during
this difficult time by promoting Take-Out Tuesdays and Thursdays on social media.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:08 P.M. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular City
Council meeting on Tuesday, December 8, 2020 at 7:00 pm for the purpose of a Regular
meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Velveth Schmitz
City Clerk  Mayor
